title: Color Don’ts
slide_intent: Make color boundaries visible so accidental effects and outdated palettes do not weaken repeated recognition.
strategic_value: Protecting the specified hues can keep Burger King applications coherent across different producers.
demonstration: Four crossed-out examples reject a palette gradient, modified colors, the previous palette and distressed red.
practical_value: Check proposed artwork for gradients, hue modifications, obsolete colors and distressing effects.

content_islands.name: Color protection rule
content_islands.spec: Place the non-modification rule and example explanation in the left column.

content_islands.name: Incorrect color treatments
content_islands.spec: Arrange four crossed-out panels at right, with a specific prohibition caption beneath each.

reference_purposes.Application: The negative examples give designers a concrete color-use review checklist.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Do not create gradients from the brand colors, modify the colors, use previous-identity colors or add distressing effects.

ingredient.name: Unmodified brand colors
ingredient.application: Keep the supplied hues flat and unaltered; reject gradients, modified hues, former palette colors and distressed effects.
ingredient.scope: Historical 2020 partner guide; the page describes these examples as illustrative rather than a complete catalog of every mistake.
